permNeeded: GeoNoMore needs permission to run on websites.
resetConfirm: All settings, rules and presets will go back to defaults. Continue?
importBad: That file could not be read.
customPointNote: This point came from the map, so it is not tied to a country. Check the time zone by hand on the Consistency tab.
consistencyIntro: A location in Türkiye with a German time zone gives you away. Everything here is fed from the same profile.
ipWarn: Your IP address is not changed. A site that checks location on its own server will still see where you really are. That needs a VPN.
modeExcept: Every site except those listed below
siteListHint: One domain per line. google.com also covers its subdomains. Where it does not run, no code is injected at all.
siteRulesHint: Use a different setting for a specific site. Empty fields fall back to the global setting. The longest matching pattern wins.
logIntro: Every setting change, every location handed to a site and everything the background does is recorded here. Copy it and send it over when something looks wrong.
logPrivacy: The log contains the sites you visited. It stays on this machine, but do look it over before sharing.
logEmpty: No records yet. Turn the extension on and visit a site that asks for your location.
exactUntilBrowser: Exact location, until the browser closes
searchFailed: The search could not be reached. Check the connection, or type the coordinates by hand.
motionNeedPoints: Add at least two points on the map to start moving.
motionRouteInfo: %1 points, %2 km, about %3 minutes per pass.
scheduleIntro: At each time below the matching preset takes over, the way your day actually moves. No background timer: which entry is in force is simply read off the clock, so it survives a sleeping browser.
schedActive: Right now the %s preset is in force.
timelineIntro: Off by default, and it should stay off unless you need it. This is a record of where you pretended to be, one point per minute, kept on this machine only.
timelineEmpty: No movement recorded yet. A point lands here only when a site actually asks for your location, so open a site that uses maps with the extension running.
domainGroupsHint: Tick a group to drop its domains into the list above. Hover to see what is in it.
spoofIpGeo: Answer IP-location lookups made by the page
coordHintFixed: Click the map to place the point.
coordHintZone: Click the map to place the centre.
zoneHintShort: On a fixed point the coordinate goes out as it is. In a zone the centre is never reported: the point sits between the two radii, dashed for the inner one and solid for the outer one.
motionIntroShort: The location walks the route instead of standing still. It keeps going even after the browser sleeps.
schedIdle: A row runs only once it has both a day and a preset.
movementIntro: Two kinds of row. Solid ones are what a site actually received. Faded ones are computed: with movement running, this is where you would have been at that minute, whether or not anyone asked.
hardeningIntro: How far the patch goes. Leave these on unless a site breaks.
hardenFrames: Follow the page into frames it creates
maskNative: Make the patched functions look built in
denyWhenOff: Where GeoNoMore is off, refuse instead of giving the real location
hardenFramesHint: A page can open an empty frame and read location from inside it, where nothing has been patched yet. Frame protection carries the patch into every same origin frame the page opens. This was the widest way out.
jitterHint: The reported point sits somewhere inside the zone and stays there for the chosen period. A point that jumps on every read gives you away faster than a point that never moves.
badgeLabel: Show the ON badge on the toolbar icon
browserHardeningHint: An extension cannot change these. They live in your browser profile and only you can set them. GeoNoMore never touches your profile.
prefsChromium: Chromium: Chrome, Edge. No about:config here, these are in settings
prefsNote: With geo.enabled set to false Firefox never reaches a location provider, so the only coordinates any site can get are the ones GeoNoMore hands over. Where GeoNoMore is off, sites then get an error rather than your real position.
mapBlocked: The map tile server is refusing requests right now. Coordinates, search and everything else still work.
tileServerHint: If the map shows blocked tiles, the tile server has blocked your address, not the extension. Switching to the other server fixes it. Both draw the same OpenStreetMap data.
lowMemoryHint: Cuts the work done on every page you open: the extension stops watching for frames the page adds later, and stops keeping a log inside the page. Location, time zone and language still change. Turn it on if you run many extensions.
ipHint: Asks a public IP service (geojs.io, then ipwho.is or freeipapi.com) where your connection appears to be. It runs only when you press it.
ipMatchTip: Your connection appears to be in %1 (%2). That matches your fake location (%3, %4).
ipMismatchTip: Your connection appears to be in %1 (%2), but your fake location says %3 (%4). Sites that look up your IP can see the difference. Use a VPN in %3, or press Match to move the fake location to %1.
trackingIntro: Signals and cleanups that apply to every site while GeoNoMore is on. They are browser settings and headers, so they switch back when you turn the extension off.
gpcHint: Tells every site "do not sell or share my data" with the Sec-GPC header and navigator.globalPrivacyControl. In some places the law requires sites to obey it.
stripParamsHint: Removes utm_*, fbclid, gclid, msclkid and similar tags from the address before the page loads. The page itself is the same; only the tag that says where you came from is gone.
noPingHint: Links with a ping attribute report each click to another address. This switches that off in the browser.
noPredictionHint: The browser looks up and preloads links before you click them. With a VPN or proxy those lookups can leave outside the tunnel. Pages may open a little slower.
noSandbox: Turn off Privacy Sandbox ad tracking
noSandboxHint: Chrome only. Switches off Topics (interests guessed from your browsing), Protected Audience (ad groups kept in your browser) and ad measurement while GeoNoMore is on.
etpAlways: Block tracking content in every window
etpAlwaysHint: Firefox only. Firefox normally blocks known tracking content in private windows only; this turns it on everywhere while GeoNoMore is on. Some embedded videos and comment boxes may stop loading.
reportingIntro: The position above is chosen. These settings decide how it reaches the site: how precise it claims to be, how often it drifts, and how often a watching site is told.
spoofIntlHint: Dates already follow the fake language. This adds numbers, currency, sorting and plural rules. On its own it rarely gives you away, but a site that sees a fake language and a real number format sees a contradiction. Turn it off if a page formats amounts oddly.
tzDeepHint: Also shifts the text a page gets from date.toString() and document.lastModified, not just the numeric readings. Without it the hour is right and the printed date is wrong, which is a contradiction of its own.
webrtcRelayHint: Stops the browser from producing local network candidates at all. A call still works if the site uses a TURN relay server, and fails if it does not. The setting above already hides your local IP without breaking anything; use this one only if you want the harder guarantee.
webrtcBlockHint: Video calls, screen sharing, some games and a few chat sites stop working. Only turn this on if you never use them.
leaksIntro: Things a page can learn about your network and your tab without asking. Each one has its own switch because each one can break something different.
fingerprintIntro: Read this before turning anything on. Adding noise is not the same as hiding. If everyone else returns the same canvas and yours comes back slightly different on every site, you are not blending into the crowd, you are standing out from it. These settings help when many people use them the same way, and hurt when you are the only one. Leave them off unless you know why you want them.
groupToggleAll: Turn everything in this group on or off
spoofWebrtcHint: WebRTC can hand a page your local network address even behind a VPN. This tells the browser not to offer it. Nothing breaks.
windowNameHint: window.name survives when you move from one site to another in the same tab, so site A can leave a marker there and site B can read it. Clearing it breaks a few old payment and login popups that use it to pass data back.
maskNativeHint: Makes the patched functions still look built in when a page prints them. Turning it off is only useful while debugging.
workerPatchHint: Pages can run code in a background worker, where the time zone and language were left real. This runs the same fix there first. Turn it off if a site stops working.
denyWhenOffHint: When the extension is off, tell sites permission was denied instead of handing over your real position. Sites that need location will refuse to work.
fpCanvasHint: A page can draw hidden text and read the pixels back; the result differs by graphics driver and font set. We change about two pixels in a hundred by one step. The picture you see is untouched, only the copy a script reads is. Photo editors and signature pads may hand back slightly altered images.
fpWebglHint: Hides the extension that reports your GPU vendor and model. Nothing else about WebGL changes, so games and maps keep working.
fpAudioHint: The audio engine produces waveforms that differ in the last decimals from machine to machine. We add a change far below hearing. Sites that edit or record audio should keep this off, since they read the same buffers.
fpRectHint: Box sizes, text width and SVG text length reveal which fonts you have installed. The shift is a fraction of a pixel and invisible, but a page that positions things by exact measurement can end up a hair off.
fpScreenHint: Reports your screen as the same size as the browser window and rounds the pixel ratio. Hides how many monitors you have, where they sit and where your taskbar is. A page that resizes itself to your screen will use the window size instead.
fpDeviceHint: Reports common values for processor cores, memory and touch points instead of yours, shows one microphone, camera and speaker to sites you have not given permission, and in Chrome also hides your connection speed and battery level. A site that sizes its worker pool by core count will pick eight.
mapWheelHint: Hold Ctrl to zoom, or click the map first
spoofNavLanguageHint: Sites read navigator.language to decide which language to show you. This reports the language of your fake location instead of your real one.
spoofAcceptLanguageHint: The same thing one level lower, in the request header the browser sends before the page even loads. Without it the server sees your real language while the page sees the fake one.
badgeLabelHint: Shows a small ON marker on the toolbar icon while the extension is running.
logMaxHint: How many log lines to keep. Older ones drop off the end.
spoofIpGeoHint: Your IP does not change and cannot. What this does is catch the page asking a service like ipapi.co and answer with the chosen country instead. A site that checks IP on its own server still sees the truth.
logDetailHint: Off, the log reads as plain sentences and hides the extension talking to itself. On, every line is shown exactly as recorded: source, event name and data. Turn it on when something is wrong and you want to report it.
logQuiet: Nothing worth reporting yet. Turn on raw output to see everything.
evtDenied: Refused %s, told it permission was denied
evtReal: Gave %s your real location (extension was off here)
evtMapBlocked: The map tile server refused the request
tileCustomHint: Paste a raster tile URL that uses {z}/{x}/{y}. This is where you plug in your own MapTiler, Thunderforest or Stadia key.
profWalkingDesc: Walks. Steady pace, short stops in between.
profRunningDesc: Runs. Faster than walking, catches its breath often.
profCyclingDesc: Rides a bike. Speeds up sometimes, slows down sometimes.
profCommutingDesc: Commutes. Medium speed with frequent stops.
profDrivingDesc: Drives a car. Fast, waits at lights.
profTrainDesc: Like a train. Very fast, stops at stations.
profFlightDesc: Like a plane. Fastest, never stops in the air.
